**What you'll do**

1. Read what the Pianet is and when it was made.
2. Learn how it makes its sound, one idea at a time.

5. Check yourself with a short quiz.

## What it is

- The **Pianet** was made by Hohner from **1962 to 1983**; the **N** from 1965 to 1968 and the N II until 1977 (Wikipedia, "Pianet").
- There is no hammer. Each key lifts a **pad** off a tuned **reed**, and the reed springs free and vibrates (Wikipedia).
- The N used leather-faced pads and a **variable-capacitance** (electrostatic) pickup; the later T used suction pads and an electromagnetic pickup (Wikipedia).

## Its sound

- Because the reed is plucked, not hit, the attack is soft, and the note dies quickly when the key comes up (Wikipedia: the reeds are damped as soon as the keys are released, said of the T).
- The N has a **vibrato switch** beside the keys and a floor **volume pedal** (Wikipedia).
- The pad's grip sets how far the reed is pulled before it lets go (this page's model).

## The panel

The Pianet's panel drawn after the real one (not a copy; no logos). Turn the knobs, flip the switches, play the keys below it,
the computer keys or a MIDI keyboard. **Simple** shows every control as a slider, including the adjustments inside the instrument.
The sound is this site's own physical model (see [how it is modelled](epiano-compare.qmd#how-each-one-is-modelled)); nobody has
compared it with the real instrument. Facts come from the Wikipedia articles listed under Works Cited (read 2026-11-26). The service manuals were not read for these pages, so control legends and places that Wikipedia does not give are marked unverified.

```{=html}
<div class="ik-box" data-kind="epiano" data-id="pianet"><div class="epc" data-model="pianet" data-compact></div></div>
```

## A guided tour

<div class="ik-step" data-set="{&quot;model&quot;:&quot;pianet&quot;}" data-riff="soul">

**The plain Pianet.** Listen: short, soft, bell-like notes.

</div>

<div class="ik-step" data-set="{&quot;model&quot;:&quot;pianet&quot;,&quot;vibOn&quot;:true}" data-riff="soul">

**Vibrato switch on.** The level wobbles at one speed (this page's rate).

</div>

<div class="ik-step" data-set="{&quot;model&quot;:&quot;pianet&quot;,&quot;pad&quot;:9,&quot;gap&quot;:8}" data-riff="soft_hard">

**A strong pad grip and the reed close to the pickup.** More bite on every note.

</div>

## Famous tracks

Each video was checked on YouTube (oEmbed, 2026-11-26). Listen first, then press **▶** for a starting setting on the panel above.

### "She's Not There" (The Zombies)

[▶ The Zombies - She&#x27;s Not There (Mono Remastered) (Official Lyric Video)](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=T6cLHNF5N8E) on YouTube (The Zombies Music).

Wikipedia names it. The famous keyboard solo and the soft, clipped chords.

<div class="ik-step" data-set="{&quot;model&quot;:&quot;pianet&quot;,&quot;pad&quot;:6}" data-riff="soul">

**Starting setting** (Pianet): pad 6. Then change it until it sounds like the record to you.

</div>

### "These Eyes" (The Guess Who)

[▶ The Guess Who - These Eyes (Official Audio)](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=xcLdbsrSngA) on YouTube (TheGuessWhoVEVO).

Wikipedia names it. Gentle chords under the verse.

<div class="ik-step" data-set="{&quot;model&quot;:&quot;pianet&quot;,&quot;pad&quot;:4,&quot;vibOn&quot;:false}" data-riff="ballad">

**Starting setting** (Pianet): pad 4, vibOn False. Then change it until it sounds like the record to you.

</div>
